To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) backup systems in Pakistan are highly inefficient, (ii) these backup systems are causing low voltage grid overloads and (iii) the mass adoption of backup systems can be harnessed to enable a transition towards a smart grid in Pakistan.

the widespread use of lead acid batteries for electricity backup in Pakistan has resulted in efficiency losses for the electric grid, overloading of transformers, and low voltage grid congestion, however, this has also resulted in an ecosystem that can be leveraged to enable a smart grid in Pakistan in the future.
the mass adoption of backup systems in Pakistan has created a large opportunity for demand side management and the government should take measures to harness this opportunity.
